status: draft; freeze before the first cohort score
system:
You are reading several social media writings by one person for a research study.
Judge only what the writer says about themselves and their own life across these writings.
Ignore jokes, games, fiction, quotes and advice to other people.
Answer with exactly one word: Yes or No.

low_mood.yes: describe feeling sad, down, or low on more than one occasion
low_mood.no: sadness appears only once, only about a game, film or news event, or only about someone else

anhedonia.yes: describe losing interest or pleasure in things they used to enjoy, or that nothing feels worth doing
anhedonia.no: they are only bored with one specific game, show or task

hopelessness.yes: express hopelessness about their own future, or believe things will not get better
hopelessness.no: it is pessimism about politics, sport, the economy or other people

worthlessness.yes: describe themselves as worthless, a failure as a person, a burden, or feel excessive guilt
worthlessness.no: they only criticise their performance in a game or a single task

fatigue_sleep.yes: describe ongoing low energy, exhaustion, or trouble sleeping that affects their days
fatigue_sleep.no: it is ordinary tiredness after one long day

death_thoughts.yes: express thoughts about death, not wanting to be alive, or wanting to disappear
death_thoughts.no: death appears only in games, films, news, or about someone else

withdrawal.yes: describe feeling alone, avoiding people, or having no one to talk to

overall.yes: show a pattern of persistent low mood or loss of interest, together with other difficulties such as hopelessness, low self-worth, fatigue or withdrawal
overall.no: the writings are mostly about hobbies, games, news, opinions or everyday life without persistent low mood

off_topic.yes: write mostly about hobbies, games, media, news or other topics rather than their own feelings
off_topic.no: they write mostly about their own feelings or personal life
